wachiman.text:
V2 canManage() is granted by VIEW on all groups, so view-only admins can create and re-parent groups

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (lines 65-71) returns true when the caller holds VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, line 70). The no-argument requireManage() is the only guard on POST /groups (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:180-181). That handler also calls realm.moveGroup(child, null) for an existing group id (GroupsResource.java:191-198). Before this PR, V2 used the base GroupPermissions.canManage(), which checks only MANAGE_USERS (GroupPermissions.java:273-276). MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:57-62) is the change that routes V2 to the new class. So an admin with only a `view` permission on the Groups resource can now create top-level groups and move any existing subgroup to the top level. No test covers this: testManageAllGroups grants MANAGE only (GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:158-160). The Javadoc at GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:72-77 documents the VIEW rule, but it contradicts canManage(GroupModel) (MANAGE only) and UserPermissionsV2.canManage(user) (MANAGE only). Fix: make V2 canManage() check MANAGE only, correct the Javadoc, and add a test where a VIEW-only admin gets 403 on POST /groups.

V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects resource IDs, not group IDs, so group-scoped view grants never restrict the user listing

(a) Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with the group ID as name and no type (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121). V1 sets type 'Group' (GroupPermissions.java:117). V2 iterates findByType(server, 'Groups') (line 121). That probably matches only the type resource, not the per-group resources. (b) Line 123 adds groupResource.getId(), the internal resource ID, not the group ID. (c) Line 122 passes that same internal ID to hasPermission(), which looks resources up by name (line 141). The lookup never finds the group resource, so it falls back to the all-groups resource (lines 143-149). The result is a set of IDs that match no group. Consequences: UsersResource.searchForUser does not set the GROUPS attribute (UsersResource.java:448-453), so the listing is not restricted and is paged before the per-user filter at UsersResource.java:460. The count endpoints call getUsersCount(..., groupIds), which returns 0 for an empty set (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/JpaUserProvider.java:634-637). A caller with VIEW_MEMBERS on a group therefore gets short or empty pages and a count that does not match the list. If the all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant applies, the bogus ID is put into GROUPS and the list is empty. No error is raised. Fix: collect and look up by resource name (the group ID), and make the iteration reach the per-group resources (for example, set a type in getOrCreateResource, or find them another way). The typing premise in (a) is the part I could not fully confirm; the ID mismatch in (b) and (c) holds either way.

testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers passes even though the GROUPS restriction is broken

With no group IDs found (see the previous finding), the query is unrestricted. The per-user filter in UsersResource.toRepresentation (UsersResource.java:460) still returns alice, so the assertion passes. The test asserts only the list, not the count endpoint or pagination, so it does not exercise the path its name describes. Add a count assertion (users().count()) or a paged search (first=0, max=1) to the same setup. There is also no coverage for VIEW-only creation of top-level groups (see the blocker).

Subgroup listing in V2 may hide subgroups that have their own permission resource, even when all-groups VIEW applies

getSubGroups now filters with auth.groups()::canView (line 179). For V2 that is GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) (GroupPermissionsV2.java:55-62), which calls hasPermission(group.getId()). The all-groups fallback (GroupPermissionsV2.java:141-150) runs only when the subgroup has no resource of its own. Before this change, an admin with all-groups VIEW saw every subgroup through canViewGlobal. Now a subgroup that has its own permission entry is hidden from that admin in this listing, while GET /groups/{id} (GroupResource.java:101) uses the same check. Is it intended that a per-group resource shadows the all-groups grant? UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same shape (UserPermissionsV2.java:105-114). If it is intended, no change is needed; if not, the shadowing needs a fix in hasPermission.

Javadoc says getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a Stream, but it returns a Set

The @return tag at line 145 says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method (line 147) returns Set<String>, and the implementations return a Set (GroupPermissions.java:298, GroupPermissionsV2.java:106). Change the tag to 'Set of IDs of groups with view permission'.

Equal order() values now pick the crypto provider by classpath order, and the multiple-provider guard is gone

Before this change, two CryptoProvider implementations on the classpath made detectProvider throw IllegalStateException. Now the stable sort at line 57 keeps ServiceLoader order whenever order() ties, and the surplus providers are only logged at debug (lines 64-70).

DefaultCryptoProvider (crypto/default/.../DefaultCryptoProvider.java:82-85), FIPS1402Provider (crypto/fips1402/.../FIPS1402Provider.java:113-116) and WildFlyElytronProvider (crypto/elytron/.../WildFlyElytronProvider.java:75-78) all return 200, so they tie.

Concrete case: integration/client-cli/client-cli-dist/pom.xml:37-56 declares keycloak-crypto-default and keycloak-crypto-fips1402 as plain dependencies, and Globals.main calls CryptoIntegration.init(cl) at integration/client-cli/admin-cli/src/main/java/org/keycloak/client/cli/common/Globals.java:44. On that classpath the provider is whichever jar comes first, and a FIPS-intended run can silently use the non-FIPS provider. The Quarkus server is not affected because KeycloakRecorder.setCryptoProvider sets the provider explicitly (quarkus/runtime/.../KeycloakRecorder.java:214-215).

Suggested fix: give the FIPS provider a higher order than the default provider so the choice is deterministic, and log ignored providers at a level that is visible by default (or keep failing on an equal top order). No test covers the new selection rule.

AuthzClient.create() installs a low-order fallback provider for the whole JVM and it cannot be replaced

CryptoIntegration.init only sets the provider when none is set (CryptoIntegration.java:29-38), so the first caller wins. AuthzClient.create() now calls it, and when AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) is the only provider visible to the authz-client classloader, it becomes the JVM-wide provider.

What breaks for other Keycloak code in that JVM:
- A later init from another classloader that does see crypto-default (order 200) is a no-op, so the order mechanism cannot help.
- AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getAesGcm/CbcCipher, getX509CertFactory, getCertificateUtils and others (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:80-97, 173-190, 203-225). Callers include PemUtils (common/.../PemUtils.java:53-135), KeyUtils.generateRsaKeyPair (common/.../KeyUtils.java:52), AbstractJWKParser (core/.../AbstractJWKParser.java:98) and JWERegistry (core/.../JWERegistry.java:55).
- getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore's provider, which is SUN (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61-67). CryptoIntegration.java:34 reads BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER when init runs, and BouncyIntegration.java:31-40 fixes it to that name, so BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER becomes "SUN" for the JVM and survives a later setProvider.

Before this change the authz client never initialised crypto, so core code in the same JVM failed with 'Please init first' (CryptoIntegration.java:46-51) unless someone else had initialised it. The regression needs the classloader split described above, hence medium confidence.

Options: do not let the fallback stay sticky (re-run detection while the current provider is this fallback); or have getBouncyCastleProvider return a real BC provider, or null as WildFlyElytronProvider.java:71-73 does.

ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key, so the P-521 (ES512) long-form DER path is never exercised

The key is generated once with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (line 42), which is a 256-bit key, and all three tests sign with it (lines 61-72). ES512 expects P-521 signatures: ECDSAAlgorithm.ES512 has signature length 132 (core/.../ECDSAAlgorithm.java:29), so r and s are 66 bytes each. With P-256, r and s stay at 32 bytes and the DER SEQUENCE stays under 128 bytes.

The long-form length branches are therefore untested: the encoder's writeLength for length > 127 (ASN1Encoder.java:66-83) and the decoder's long-form readLength (ASN1Decoder.java:137-164). Only a P-521 signature reaches them. testES512 and testES384 pass without touching the code that most needs coverage.

Fix: generate a key per algorithm with the matching curve (secp384r1 for ES384, secp521r1 for ES512) via KeyPairGenerator.initialize(new ECGenParameterSpec(...)).

The round-trip assertion accepts a DER encoding that a JDK verifier would reject

The test only checks RS -> DER -> RS consistency (lines 53-56). The DER output is fed back into the same new decoder and never checked against the JDK. A broken encoder can still pass, for example one that drops the 0x00 sign byte when r or s has its top bit set: the decoder reads the INTEGER back as a negative BigInteger, and integerToBytes (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:151-163) restores the same 32 bytes, so assertArrayEquals still passes.

Suggestion: assert that the re-encoded DER equals the JDK's output (assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)), or verify asn1Des with java.security.Signature against the public key.

Dead statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER

Lines 114-115 build two ASN1Encoder instances and discard them. The return at lines 117-121 builds the sequence independently, so these two calls have no effect. Remove them.

hamcrest test dependency is unused

The new org.hamcrest:hamcrest test dependency is not used. ECDSAAlgorithmTest imports only org.junit.Assert and org.junit.Test (ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:27-28). Drop the dependency, or use a hamcrest matcher if one is intended.

order() is added as an abstract method, breaking out-of-tree CryptoProvider implementations

Any CryptoProvider implementation outside this repository stops compiling until it adds order(). The interface already gives defaults to newer methods (getSupportedKeyStoreTypes at line 104, getSupportedRsaKeySizes at line 137). Consider a default implementation, for example returning 0, so existing providers keep compiling. The four in-repo providers already implement it.

PR body does not describe the behaviour changes

The PR body is one line: 'Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations'. The diff also changes how the JVM-wide crypto provider is selected (CryptoIntegration.java:56-71), adds an abstract order() API (CryptoProvider.java:44), and makes AuthzClient.create() initialise crypto (AuthzClient.java:95). AuthzClientCryptoProvider implements only the ECDSA conversion, getKeyStore and getBouncyCastleProvider; the rest throw UnsupportedOperationException (lines 74-97). Worth stating in the description.

getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a missing group, which breaks the GroupModel contract

The NPE is replaced by `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount()`. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount is documented as "Never returns null" (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:296). The PR body does not mention this change of contract.

What a caller sees: RealmCacheSession.getGroupById returns a cached adapter without checking the database when the entry is cached and not invalidated (model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/RealmCacheSession.java:964-985). For a group whose row is already gone, the group is still listed, and populateSubGroupCount stores null (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:90). The admin UI tests the count with `!== 0` (js/apps/admin-ui/src/components/group/GroupPickerDialog.tsx:324), so null is not read as zero.

Before, the request failed with an NPE. Now it succeeds silently with a removed group still listed and no count. Either the null is accepted and GroupModel's contract is updated, or the stale entry is dropped or the group omitted. That choice belongs to the author.

The same concurrent NPE remains in the sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads

The title says the PR prevents NullPointerException under concurrent group access. The same unguarded pattern remains in this file: `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` at lines 256, 262 and 268 has no null check. This path is reached from services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:180 (`group.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)`). If the group row was removed while its cached adapter is still served, that call throws the same NPE the PR fixes for getSubGroupsCount.

The guard for these methods needs a decision on what to return (for example an empty stream), so the author should either apply it here or state that these are out of scope.

Reader thread is never stopped on failure and is not joined before the assertion

Two problems in the new test:

1. `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) runs only if every `remove()` in lines 152-154 succeeds. If one throws, the test fails but the reader thread (lines 139-149), created with the default non-daemon status, loops forever and keeps sending admin requests. That can hang the JVM or leave load on the shared test server.
2. The thread is not joined, so the assertion at line 157 can run while the reader is still inside a request. An exception raised by that last request is then missed.

Fix: put the delete loop and the flag in try/finally, join the reader thread, and only then assert on `caughtExceptions`.

Does this test fail on the pre-fix code?

The reader only checks that no exception escapes the listing call. The NPE needs a cached group whose database row is already removed, which means the window between the delete and the cache invalidation. Nothing in the test forces that window, so the test may pass on the code before the GroupAdapter change. I did not run it (the review is read-only). Did you confirm that it fails without the fix? If the timing is too narrow, a deterministic setup would be better.

Test name and variable name do not describe the regression

`createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` says nothing about concurrent reads during deletes, and it has no reference to the bug (the PR body does not name an issue). The variable `groupUuuids` (lines 121, 129, 152) has a typo. A name such as `listGroupsWhileDeletingConcurrently` and a short comment linking the NPE would make the intent clear.

Unrelated dead-code removal in a concurrency fix

The private method `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` was removed. It had no callers in this file, and the diff does not touch any caller, so the removal is safe. It is unrelated to the NPE fix, though. Consider moving it to its own change or mentioning it in the PR body.

Parent lookup can return null here; does the hierarchy path still throw on concurrent removal?

Line 47 takes `parentModel` from `session.groups().getGroupById(...)` without a null check. Lines 51 and 56-57 then pass it to `canView` and `toRepresentation`. If the parent row is gone and not cached, the cache returns null (RealmCacheSession.java:973), and this path would throw the NPE the PR is meant to remove. The dereference inside `ModelToRepresentation` is not confirmed here, so this is a question about the author's intent, not a verified defect. Does the concurrency fix need to cover this path too?

UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no argument; services does not compile

`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` calls a zero-argument overload. The only definition in the repository is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 (grep for the name finds no other definition). The services module therefore fails to compile, and nothing in this PR can be built or tested. The predicate is meant to be passkeys-enabled only (the comment above it says 'skip the form when user is re-authenticating' unless passkeys are on), so the fix is the one in the next finding: make the method take no argument and check only `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`.

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) returns false when no user is set, which removes passkey data from the first login page and from the invalid-username path

The old code filled webauthn data only when `context.getUser() == null` (base lines 110-112 inside the else branch; base challenge(error, field) at line 136). The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so the condition is inverted for the no-user case. Concretely: (1) authenticate() at lines 114-117 with user null (ordinary login page) no longer calls fillContextForm, so ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI is not set; login.ftl:16 and login-username.ftl:22 then render autocomplete='username' instead of 'username webauthn', and the conditional passkey block in passkeys.ftl:2 is skipped. (2) challenge(error, field) at lines 136-141 is reached with user null on an invalid username (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:109 testInvalidUser) and no longer fills. The PR's own tests assert the opposite: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:145 and :195, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:183, :190 and :241, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:192 and :250 all expect 'username webauthn' on the first page. Those assertions would fail. The re-authentication path (user set) is the only case the new code handles. The fix is to drop the user parameter and the `user != null` clause so that the helper means 'passkeys enabled', which also resolves the compile error above. Callers at lines 115 and 137 then fill in both cases, as the tests expect.

After a wrong password on the username-then-password flow, PasswordForm now renders passkey data, but its first render does not

PasswordForm extends UsernamePasswordForm and is constructed with a session (PasswordForm.java:35-37), so webauthnAuth is non-null. PasswordForm.authenticate() (PasswordForm.java:45-52) renders the password page without calling fillContextForm. The error path, however, goes through challenge(context, error, field) (UsernamePasswordForm.java:136-141), and with the user set it now fills the passkey data. A wrong password on that page therefore shows passkey data that the first render did not. No test in this PR covers PasswordForm. Is that intended? If not, PasswordForm should override the error path as it already overrides authenticate().

NoSuchElementException import is unused after the assertThrows lines were replaced

The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls (base lines 199 and 210) were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., notNullValue())`. Grep finds no other use of `NoSuchElementException` in this file, so the import at line 51 is dead.

PasswordCredentialModel is imported but never used in this file

The import at line 35 is not referenced anywhere in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java (grep finds only the import). Remove it.

Negative webauthn checks catch every Exception, so they pass on any driver error

In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (lines 291-296 and 312-317), the absence of the webauthn form is checked with `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { }`. Any exception from findElement passes the check, including a stale element or a session error, so the assertion does not prove the form is absent. A check such as `driver.findElements(By.xpath(...)).isEmpty()` would assert what the comment says, and the existing `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` pattern in PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:202 is narrower.

Re-authentication no longer skips the username form for every user when passkeys are enabled, not just for users with a passkey

Before this PR, UsernameForm skipped the form on re-authentication (context.success() at line 50) unless the user had linked brokers. With `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (once the predicate is fixed to be passkeys-only), the skip is also disabled for password-only users in a passkey-enabled realm. The new tests cover re-authentication with passkeys enabled only for users with a passkey (PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:259-321) and the no-passkey case only with passkeys disabled at realm level (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:277-333). A password-only user in a passkey-enabled realm is not covered. Is it intended that such a user now sees the username form on prompt=login?

Hung spawned flusher is never killed on restart, so two flushers run on the same shards

The base code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (inside `try/except ValueError`). The new code gates it on `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Production processes come from `self.mp_context.Process` where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` (flusher.py:53, 105). In CPython, the spawn-context class `SpawnProcess` derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process`, so the check is False and `kill()` never runs on the production path. I could not re-read the stdlib from this workspace to confirm that hierarchy, so this rests on CPython's source as I know it.

Effect: when `healthy_since` goes stale, `_create_process_for_shards` (flusher.py:259) starts a replacement on the same shards, but the hung process keeps running. Both processes then flush the same Redis queues, and duplicate segments can be produced to buffered-segments. Each restart also leaves one more live process behind until `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`.

Fix: gate on `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or go back to calling `process.kill()` in `try/except (ValueError, AttributeError)`. The same `isinstance(..., multiprocessing.Process)` check at flusher.py:346 in `join()` is inherited from the base, so `terminate()` also never fires for spawned processes; the same fix applies there.

`_create_process_for_shard` is dead code

Nothing calls `_create_process_for_shard` (singular). The only callers are `_create_processes` and `_ensure_processes_alive`, and both use the plural `_create_process_for_shards`. Remove it, or use it if a per-shard restart was intended.

Class docstring says one process per shard, but the default is one process

The docstring says "Creates one process per shard". The consumer default is `--flusher-processes` 1 (consumers/__init__.py:432-437), which gives a single process owning all shards, the same as before this change. One process per shard only happens when `max_processes` is None, which is the direct-construction default. Make the docstring say that the number of processes is capped by `max_processes` and that the consumer defaults to 1.

Memory check runs one cluster-wide INFO per buffer on every submit

`submit()` now loops over every per-process buffer and calls `buffer.get_memory_info()` (flusher.py:300-301). Each call goes to `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:375-376), which issues `cluster.info()` to every node (src/sentry/processing/backpressure/memory.py:82-97). All buffers share the same Redis cluster (`get_redis_client()`, buffer.py:117-118), so with N processes each submit makes N full cluster INFO round-trips and the `memory_infos` list holds N copies of the same data. The used/available ratio stays correct, because the copies cancel out. Read memory from one buffer, or keep one buffer for this check.

`--flusher-processes` accepts values the flusher cannot handle

The option has no minimum. A negative value makes `num_processes` negative (flusher.py:60), so `process_to_shards_map` is empty and the loop at flusher.py:64-66 raises KeyError when the consumer starts. The error does not say what went wrong. A value of 0 is swallowed by `max_processes or len(...)` (flusher.py:51), so it silently means one process per shard. Use `click.IntRange(min=1)` for this option, and consider validating the value in the factory.

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op in this test

`test_basic` calls `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 does nothing. The comment on line 61 says the wait gives flusher threads time to run after the drift change, but no wait happens. `step.join()` at line 64 sets `stopped` right away, and the flusher thread can exit before it flushes. Then `(msg,) = messages` fails. The test is still racy. Wait for the flush explicitly, for example by polling `messages` with a real clock, or restore `time.sleep` for this wait.

`test_flusher_processes_limit` never runs the process path it is meant to cover

The test passes `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, so `SpanFlusher` starts `threading.Thread` workers (flusher.py:107-108) and never spawns processes. It therefore does not cover the spawn path that the `kill`/`terminate` gating depends on, and it does not cover the restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive`. It only checks counts (`len(processes)`, `num_processes`, total shards). Add a test that exercises restart, or at least check which shards each process gets.

New rule bans `hasattr()` for unions, which the codebase uses widely

The rule is unrelated to this PR, and it is stated more broadly than the code supports. `hasattr(` appears 226 times across 135 files under src/sentry. `hasattr` duck-typing is a common, idiomatic pattern here, and no linter enforces this rule. The example also does not show a defect, because `isinstance` and `hasattr` give the same result for `str | None`. Drop the rule from this PR, or narrow it to a concrete case you have seen cause a bug.

Metric tag keys and values are inconsistent

`spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses the tag key `shards` (line 199), while `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `shard` (lines 185, 195). The `shard` tag on `produce` holds a comma-joined list such as "0,1,2", but `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) emits one value per shard as an int. Dashboards that group by `shard` will mix per-shard and per-process series. Use one key and decide whether the value is one shard or one process group.

`spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` is now a budget per process, not a total

Each process calls `buffer.flush_segments(now=now)` on its own shard subset (flusher.py:169). `flush_segments` sizes its budget from that subset (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-384), so each process can flush up to `max-flush-segments` per cycle. Total flush volume per cycle therefore grows with the number of processes. Is this intended? If so, document it on the option. If the cap should stay global, divide the budget by the number of processes.

Error events are repeated and misplaced across summary pages

`analyze_recording_segments` is passed to `paginate` via `functools.partial` (line 100), so it runs once per page with only that page's segments. `GenericOffsetPaginator` calls `data_fn(offset=..., limit=...)` per page (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:524). `gen_request_data` starts `error_idx = 0` on every call (line 146) and, after the segment loop, yields every remaining error (lines 164-168). An error earlier than a page's first event is emitted at the start of that page, and every error after a page's last event is emitted at the end of that page, so the same error can appear in several pages' summary inputs. Limit errors to the page's time window, or emit each error once across the replay. Confidence is medium because I did not read the `paginate` helper that calls `on_results`.

Error lookup runs on every page request and the nodestore read is unchunked

`get` runs `query_replay_instance` (Snuba) and then `fetch_error_details` (nodestore) before `self.paginate` (lines 70-94), so each page request repeats the whole-replay error lookup. `fetch_error_details` passes every error ID to one `nodestore.backend.get_multi` call (line 108), with no chunking. `bulk_fetch_events` in delayed_workflow.py:453-455 chunks the same kind of call by EVENT_LIMIT. Consider caching the error list per replay or running the lookup for the first page only, and chunking the nodestore read.

Error `id` is paired with the wrong nodestore value when a node is missing

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs IDs with dict values by position. If `get_multi` omits missing node IDs rather than returning None for them, each later `id` is attached to the wrong event. The `id` field is not used in `generate_error_log_message` (lines 126-131), so the summary text is unaffected today. Look up each event by its node ID instead of zipping.

Storage deletion errors are dropped silently while the replay is archived

`pool.map(_delete_if_exists, ...)` returns a lazy iterator. Exceptions raised by the workers are only re-raised when the results are iterated, and nothing iterates here. `_delete_if_exists` only handles `NotFound` (lines 80-83), so any other storage error (timeouts, 5xx, rate limits) is lost. `delete_matched_rows` then calls `delete_replays`, which archives the replays (lines 58-61). Recording blobs can remain with no log and no error returned to the user. Collect the futures and re-raise or count failures, or iterate the results so errors surface.

One invalid report now rejects the whole batch, including its valid reports

The throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26), so it covers the whole URL including the query string. invalid_host? checks only the host (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15), so any path or query on the embeddable host is accepted. An unauthenticated client can therefore cause unbounded feed downloads and outbound requests. Suggested fix: key the throttle on the feed or host rather than the full URL, or rate-limit the enqueue.
